title: The ledger names a run whose findings.json it cannot read instead of dropping its rows
body:
## Summary
uat/driver/ledger.cjs turned an unreadable or non-list findings.json into zero rows with no word on OPEN.md.

## Description
ledger() read each run record in a try/catch that set the rows to [] on any parse error (uat/driver/ledger.cjs:71 before the fix), and a non-array was silently treated as empty. writeBack() and synthesize() rewrite findings.json whole (uat/driver/recertify.cjs:186, uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:346), so a torn write is reachable. OPEN.md then showed fewer open gaps and nothing said why: a load failure indistinguishable from "nothing open" (registry eval-harness, _laws failure-not-empty-success). Fixed: ledger() returns unreadable: [{ run, error }] and statusOf() prints one `unreadable: <run>/findings.json (...)` line per such run.

## Flow
- a run record is torn or replaced by an object
- node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --status
- before: its open rows vanish from OPEN.md silently; after: OPEN.md names the run and the parse error

## Expected impact
The operator reading OPEN.md can no longer mistake a damaged record for a drained one. Nothing changes for readable runs (committed runs: unreadable []).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a damaged run record is named, never read as empty
Before: 0 of 2 seeded unreadable runs named on OPEN.md
After: 2 of 2 named (new case in tools/uat-ledger-test.cjs, red -> green)
Method: gate - a test seeded with a torn file and an object
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A Character process that exits non-zero is reported as crashed even when its file reads
body:
## Summary
The LT parent marked a Character crashed only when its <id>.json was missing, so a child that died after saving some journeys read as finished and the run exited 0.

## Description
child() saves after every journey (uat/driver/linga-text.cjs save()), and the parent read results with `try { JSON.parse(...) } catch { crashed }`, ignoring the exit code it had collected. A process that died in journey 3 left a readable file of two journeys: the scorecard showed two rows and no crash row, and `results.some(r => r.crashed)` was false, so the run exited 0 (registry eval-harness: a crash is not a low score). Fixed: collectResults(dir, cast, codes) marks any non-zero exit crashed with its exit code and keeps the journeys it saved.

## Flow
- a Character child throws an unhandled error in its third journey after saving two
- parent reads <id>.json
- before: complete-looking result, exit 0; after: crashed (exit 1) with its two journeys, report crash row, exit 1

## Expected impact
A partial LT run is no longer reported as a complete one. Could break: nothing reads a crashed result differently except the scorecard crash row and the exit code.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a dead Character process is reported as a crash
Before: saved-then-died Character read as crashed: no; parent exit 0
After: crashed: yes, exit 1, J1 kept (new case in tools/uat-verdict-test.cjs, red -> green)
Method: gate - unit test of the extracted collectResults() with exits 0 / 1 / null
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:265 (before): const results = cast.map((c, i) => { try { return JSON.parse(...) } catch { return { ..., crashed: true, exit: codes[i] } } })
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:571 save() after each journey
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:276 process.exit(results.some(r => r.crashed) ? 1 : 0)

title: --run refuses a run id that already holds findings.json instead of writing over it
body:
## Summary
`--run <id>` naming an existing run overwrote its run.json, Character files, reports and findings.json, the record the ledger and recertify stamps live in.

## Description
Without --run the parent picks a free id (uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:236-237); with --run it used the id as given (dir = path.join(runsDir, id)) and rewrote everything in it after a paid run, mixing the old run's other Characters into the new one. Fixed: parseArgs() throws before anything is spawned when <runs>/<id>/findings.json exists, and names --recertify.

## Flow
- node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --run 2026-10-09-lt
- before: run.json, <id>.json, report.md, SUMMARY.md, findings.json of the committed run are overwritten
- after: refused before spawning, naming --recertify

## Expected impact
The operator cannot destroy a run record (and its recertify stamps) by reusing an id. A directory with no findings.json is still accepted.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a run record is never overwritten by a new run
Before: --run <existing> accepted (8 committed findings.json reachable)
After: refused (new case in tools/uat-ledger-test.cjs, red -> green)
Method: gate - parseArgs test over a temp runs dir
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:235-238 id = runId ?? `${day}-lt` ...; dir = path.join(runsDir, id)
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:346 fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "findings.json"), ...)
git ls-files uat/runs | grep findings.json -> 8 files

title: recertify reads Character files through the ledger reader, so one torn file no longer loses every stamp
body:
## Summary
ledger.cjs and recertify.cjs each carried their own per-Character result reader and isOpen; the recertify copy threw on one unreadable file and finish() lost the whole rerun.

## Description
ledger.cjs resultsOf skipped a file it could not parse (uat/driver/ledger.cjs:54-55); recertify.cjs results() parsed without a guard (uat/driver/recertify.cjs:32 before). A child that dies while saving leaves a torn <id>.json, and finish() then threw a SyntaxError before writeBack(): every judge answer of the paid rerun was lost and recertify.md never written, although finish() already maps a planned pair with no judged result to not-evaluable (uat/driver/recertify.cjs:276-278). Fixed: recertify takes results via ledger.resultsOf (exported) and isOpen from the ledger.

## Flow
- a ledger or per-run recertify where one Character process dies while saving
- finish(prior, rerun)
- before: SyntaxError, 0 rows stamped; after: the pair's open rows stamped not-evaluable, recertify.md written

## Expected impact
A crash in one Character no longer throws away the answers of every other Character in the rerun. Could break: a malformed file is now skipped in metric deltas too, which is what the ledger already did.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one torn result file cannot lose a rerun's stamps
Before: finish() throws; copies of the reader and of isOpen in uat/driver: 2 and 2
After: finish() stamps the pair not-evaluable; 1 and 1 (new case in tools/uat-recertify-test.cjs, red -> green)
Method: gate - test with a torn tomas-9.json in a rerun of a temp copy of the beginners run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/driver/recertify.cjs:30-35 (before): NOT_RESULTS, results = ... .map(f => readJson(...)), isOpen = f => f.type !== ...
uat/driver/ledger.cjs:30,54-55: NOT_RESULTS, resultsOf with try/catch
red run: SyntaxError: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 45

title: The run instrument hashes every driver file in the directory, not a hand-kept list
body:
## Summary
instrumentOf() hashed a literal list of seven driver files into run.json; a driver file added later would run unrecorded until the list was edited by hand.

## Description
The instrument lets a recertify tell a driver change from a product change (uat/driver/recertify.cjs instrumentOf). The list matched the directory (7 of 7) but was grown by hand three times (a8c8b291, 9a9cdb9e, 31ba670f). Fixed: the list is read from the directory (every .cjs, sorted); instrumentOf takes an optional dir so the derivation is tested with a seeded extra file.

## Flow
- a new uat/driver/<x>.cjs lands without editing instrumentOf
- a run writes run.json
- before: <x>.cjs absent from instrument.driver, so a change to it reads as no instrument change; after: hashed

## Expected impact
Recertify confounds stay complete as the driver grows. Hashes of the existing seven are identical, so older runs compare equal on those keys.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the instrument covers the whole driver
Before: seeded driver file in the instrument: no (7 of 7 today by hand)
After: yes; .md ignored; same blobs hash the same (new case in tools/uat-recertify-test.cjs, red -> green)
Method: gate - test over a copy of the driver dir plus a seeded .cjs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/driver/recertify.cjs:331 (before): ['linga-text.cjs', 'surface.cjs', 'recertify.cjs', 'verdict.cjs', 'ledger.cjs', 'metrics.cjs', 'product.cjs'].map(...)
git log -S on that list: a8c8b291, 9a9cdb9e, 31ba670f

title: --journeys refuses an id no journey file defines instead of an empty run that exits 0
body:
## Summary
A --journeys typo matched no Character's list, so every child ran zero journeys, the run exited 0 and an empty run directory landed under uat/runs.

## Description
child() runs C.journeys filtered by UAT_JOURNEYS (uat/driver/linga-text.cjs `mine`); an id no file defines filters everything out. The parent then wrote an empty findings.json, which the ledger counts as an undrained run. parseArgs() already stops on an unknown metric gate before spawning; it now does the same for an unknown --journeys id and names the known ones.

## Flow
- node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --journeys J1,J7
- before: every child runs J1 only, or nothing for --journeys J7, run exits 0; after: refused before spawning, naming J7 and the known ids

## Expected impact
An operator typo costs nothing and leaves no empty run behind. The committed J1-J5 are all accepted.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a mistyped journey id stops the run before it starts
Before: `--journeys J1,J7` accepted
After: refused naming J7 (new case in tools/uat-metrics-test.cjs, red -> green)
Method: gate - parseArgs test with injected journey texts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs child(): const mine = C.journeys.filter(j => !selection.length || selection.includes(j))
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs parseArgs(): only unknownGates was checked before spawn

title: OPEN.md states the open total, and says 0 when nothing is open
body:
## Summary
statusOf() printed counts only inside module sections, so with nothing open OPEN.md showed no count at all.

## Description
A module with no open row has no section (uat/driver/ledger.cjs section()), so a zero-open ledger rendered the title, preamble and drained line only: indistinguishable from a page whose sections failed. Fixed: an always-present `<n> open across <m> runs` line, with ": nothing to recertify" at 0.

## Flow
- every gap fixed or a strength
- node uat/driver/linga-text.cjs --status
- before: no count on the page; after: "0 open across 1 run: nothing to recertify"

## Expected impact
The operator view answers its main question in the empty state. Existing lines unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the empty state is said, not implied
Before: zero-open ledger: no count line
After: "0 open across 1 run: nothing to recertify"; committed runs "186 open across 5 runs" (new case in tools/uat-ledger-test.cjs, red -> green)
Method: gate - statusOf over a temp run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: uat/driver/ledger.cjs statusOf(): section = mod => { const open = ...; if (!open.length) return []; ... }

title: The surface catalogue's Linga screen list is held to the session store's Screen type
body:
## Summary
surface.cjs walked a literal list of 12 Linga screens with nothing comparing it to store.ts `Screen`.

## Description
catalogue() (uat/driver/surface.cjs) walks LINGA_SCREENS to name a phone control the current screen no longer offers. Its ground truth is the Linga members of `export type Screen` (desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:35). They agree today (12 and 12); a new Linga screen would have been left out and its controls read as strays. Fixed: exported, and a guard in tools/uat-surface-test.cjs reads the type (comments stripped) and requires equality, with an in-test seeded control.

## Flow
- a new "linga-x" screen is added to Screen
- before: catalogue never walks it; after: uat-surface-test goes red

## Expected impact
The phone-only drift detector stays complete as Linga grows.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a hand list is held to its ground truth
Before: guards comparing the 12 walked screens to the 12 declared: 0
After: 1, seeded extra screen detected (red -> green)
Method: gate - guard test with a seeded control
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/driver/surface.cjs: const LINGA_SCREENS = ['linga', 'linga-check', ... 'linga-certs'] (12)
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:35 export type Screen = ... 12 linga members

title: Accepted gap AG-5 no longer says LT answers on codex
body:
## Summary
uat/accepted-gaps.md AG-5 said LT model responses come from codex and claude is kept for manual tests; since 2026-10-09 every LT role runs on the claude CLI.

## Description
The driver refuses codex and runs tutor, Character, judge and synthesis on the claude CLI (uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:21-24, :45-47; uat/README.md:21; uat/env.md:20). AG-5 is in the list a run reads to decide what not to re-raise. Fixed: the row is marked retired with the date and keeps its ceiling only for the 2026-09-15 codex runs. No replacement gap was invented.

## Flow
- a reader or a judge consults accepted-gaps.md
- before: told LT answers on codex; after: told AG-5 is retired and why

## Expected impact
Nobody acts on a stale engine claim. Whether the same-family judge bias becomes an accepted gap stays the owner's call.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no accepted gap contradicts the driver
Before: 1 statement contradicted by the driver
After: 0
Method: probe - the row read against linga-text.cjs, README and env.md
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/accepted-gaps.md:11 (before): | AG-5 | Model responses at LT come from codex ... | Owner's choice: claude is kept for manual tests.
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:46 refuseCodexEngine()

title: README layout names metrics.cjs and its readBlock anchor points at readBlock
body:
## Summary
uat/README.md listed six of seven driver files and cited linga-text.cjs:38-44 for a throw that lives at :51-55.

## Description
The Layout block omitted driver/metrics.cjs, the registry every judge schema, gate, roll-up and report line derive from. The anchor for "the LT driver throws on a top-level file without one" pointed at ROLES/refuseCodexEngine. Fixed both.

## Flow
- a reader follows README to the driver
- before: metrics.cjs unlisted and the anchor lands on the wrong function; after: both match the tree

Readers find the metric registry and the right throw.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - README matches the tree
Before: 2 statements contradicted (6 of 7 files listed)
After: 0 (7 of 7)
Method: probe - ls uat/driver and sed -n 51,55p uat/driver/linga-text.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The run record is rewritten in place, so a crash mid-write tears findings.json
body:
## Summary
writeBack(), synthesize() and the ledger rerun rewrite findings.json with a plain writeFileSync, not a write-then-rename.

## Description
findings.json is the record every recertify stamp lives in (uat/driver/recertify.cjs:186 writeBack, uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:346 synthesize). A process killed during the write leaves a truncated file. Since f463deb2 the ledger names such a run instead of hiding it, but the rows are still lost until restored from git, and an uncommitted recertify stamp is lost for good. "Fixed" is a temp file in the same directory then fs.renameSync over the record.

## Flow
- finishLedger() stamps five runs; the operator interrupts during the third write
- before: the third findings.json is torn and its stamps gone
- after (proposed): the old or the new record, never half

## Expected impact
Recertify stamps survive an interrupted write. Could break: renameSync over an open file on Windows can fail (EPERM) if another process holds it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the record is replaced atomically
Before: writes of findings.json that can tear: 3 sites (writeBack, synthesize, OPEN.md is derived so excluded)
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - a kill during writeFileSync cannot be taken on this tree without a fault-injection seam; three walked cases: Ctrl-C during finishLedger, a child OOM during synthesize, a power loss
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
uat/driver/recertify.cjs:186 fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(rows, null, 2))
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:346 fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "findings.json"), ...)
instrument: a fault-injection test: stub fs.writeFileSync to write half the bytes then throw for findings.json, call writeBack(), and assert the original record still parses (red today, green with temp+rename)

title: The context map omits three uat files: metrics.cjs, product.cjs and uat-metrics-test
body:
## Summary
context-map.json lists five of the seven uat/driver files and four of the five uat suites.

## Description
uat/driver/metrics.cjs (the metric registry), uat/driver/product.cjs (the product stamp) and tools/uat-metrics-test.cjs exist and are loaded by linga-text, ledger and recertify, but the uat context's file_paths (context-map.json:533-563) do not name them, so a sweep or a coverage tool never assigns them to a context. Editing the map is an architecture act the director owns.

## Flow
- coverage.mjs or a round reads the uat context
- metrics.cjs, product.cjs and uat-metrics-test.cjs are in no context

## Expected impact
The three files get swept and counted. Nothing in the product changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every uat file belongs to a context
Before: 3 uat files in no context (driver 5 of 7, suites 4 of 5)
After: 0 (add them to the uat context)
Method: probe - ls uat/driver and tools/uat-*-test.cjs against context-map.json
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
context-map.json:533-563 uat file_paths
ls uat/driver: ledger linga-text metrics product recertify surface verdict
ls tools/uat-*: ledger metrics recertify surface verdict

title: The sweep overlay still says a live LT run costs codex calls
body:
## Summary
.claude/scan-sweep/config.md (the uat/driver gate row) and this run's brief say a live LT run costs codex calls; it costs claude CLI subscription calls.

## Description
Since the operator rule of 2026-10-09 the driver refuses codex and every role runs on the claude CLI (uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:21-24, :45-47). The overlay is director-owned and outside this round's paths. "Fixed" is the gate row reading: a live LT run spends claude CLI subscription calls and is the operator's call.

## Flow
- a builder reads the overlay before touching uat/driver
- before: told the cost is codex; after: told the real engine

## Expected impact
Builders reason about the real cost and engine.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the overlay matches the driver
Before: 1 stale engine claim in the overlay
After: 0
Method: probe - overlay line read against linga-text.cjs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
.claude/scan-sweep/config.md:34 | `uat/driver` | ... a live LT run costs codex calls ...
uat/driver/linga-text.cjs:22 "no codex, no paid API"
instrument: out-of-scope (director-owned overlay): grep -n codex .claude/scan-sweep/config.md returns 0 lines on the gate row after the edit
note: director: overlay edited at wave 2 integration
